article_title: No significant changes in synaptic density and gray matter volume following motor learning—a pilot study
citation: Hehl, M., Toyonaga, T., Carson, R. E., Dupont, P., Van Laere, K., Swinnen, S. P. & Cuypers, K. (2026). No significant changes in synaptic density and gray matter volume following motor learning—a pilot study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00451-5
title: Bimanual tracking task (BTT) four-week motor learning paradigm
description: The bimanual tracking task is a laboratory motor-learning paradigm in which participants track a visual target moving along a target line by rotating two dials with the left and right index fingers, controlling the vertical and horizontal movements of a cursor. Performance is scored per trial as a percentage from 0–100% reflecting accuracy in speed, movement direction and distance from the target, with on-screen score feedback after each trial. In this study, "participants were stratiﬁed by sex and pseudo-randomly assigned to either a complex or a simple training group", training four sessions per week of 30 min for four weeks, with an individually adapting staircase-like level paradigm for the complex group and a standardized 18-task progress test administered six times.
requirements: The task can be adapted to participants' improving skill levels over time to secure continuing motivation and challenge; the complex group requires an individually adapting staircase-like level paradigm
constraints: The article notes the task was chosen as a novel task not part of the daily motor repertoire, and that GM changes with motor learning had not yet been examined for the BTT specifically
target_learners: young healthy adult volunteers (mean age 24.7 years)
examples: Training adherence was 99.7 ± 0.76% with no significant difference between the two training groups
key_sources: Hehl, M., Toyonaga, T., Carson, R. E., Dupont, P., Van Laere, K., Swinnen, S. P. & Cuypers, K. (2026). No significant changes in synaptic density and gray matter volume following motor learning—a pilot study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00451-5

article_title: Instructor-learner body coupling reflects instruction and learning
citation: Yafeng Pan, Suzanne Dikker, Yi Zhu, Cuirong Yang, Yi Hu and Pavel Goldstein. (2022). Instructor-learner body coupling reflects instruction and learning. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00131-0
title: Body-to-Body Coupling (BtBC) via Motion Energy Analysis as a measure of pedagogical interaction
description: The article introduces BtBC as a dyadic measure derived from video-based Motion Energy Analysis, "a computer-vision method based on the assessment of differences in sequences of frames in video recordings, requiring no motion capture devices on instructors or learners". Motion in instructor and learner ROIs is cross-correlated over 30-s moving windows across 251 time lags, yielding an overall BtBC index averaged over all lags. The framework positions "the real-time interaction of teaching and learning bodies" as important for learning, with instructional approach shaping whether coupling emerges.
requirements: A high-definition video recording of the instructor-learner interaction from which motion energy can be extracted for pre-defined regions of interest
constraints: MEA uses fixed pre-defined ROIs and cannot track moving ROIs or movement details; findings are correlational, from same-gender (female-female) dyads, and require replication with larger samples
target_learners: adult learners in dyadic instructor-learner interactions
target_learning_goals: conceptual learning of psychological concepts (e.g., reinforcement and transfer)
examples: In the reported experiment, 48 female participants formed 24 instructor-learner dyads teaching reinforcement and transfer concepts under scaffolding and explanation approaches, with BtBC quantified from video using the rMEA package
key_sources: Yafeng Pan, Suzanne Dikker, Yi Zhu, Cuirong Yang, Yi Hu and Pavel Goldstein. (2022). Instructor-learner body coupling reflects instruction and learning. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00131-0

article_title: Developing Digital Competences Using an Educational Software. A Pedagogical Research
citation: Ioana Magdaş, Timea Bontea. (2011). Developing digital competences using an educational software. A pedagogical research. Acta Didactica Napocensia, Volume 4, Number 4, ISSN 2065-1430. https://www.moodle.ro
title: BT Access Database: a Moodle-built course for developing digital competences in databases and Microsoft Access 2007
description: An educational software course built on the open-source Moodle platform (via www.edu.moodle.ro) for XII-grade technical-college students, covering the baccalaureate Databases unit. The article states "The software developed is a course called BT Access Database . A course can contain resources and activities." It uses LABEL for information, RESOURCE for Word documents and PowerPoint presentations, a video created with Adobe Captivate about creating databases, TESTS, LESSONs, CHAT, FORUM, CHOICE, WIKI, ASSIGNMENTS, WORKSHOPS, GLOSSARY and an "Upload a single file" option for checking Access activities. Moodle is described as a course management system designed on constructivist principles, used by over 34 million users in over 200 countries and available in over 70 languages.
requirements: Moodle must be installed on a server and is accessible from any computer connected to the Internet; an administrator monitors each installed platform
constraints: developed specifically for the Romanian baccalaureate digital-skills examination and adapted for Technical Colleges
target_learners: XII-grade students of technical profile / technological high-schools
target_learning_goals: database theory and use of Microsoft Office Access 2007; preparation for the baccalaureate digital-skills exam
examples: A partnership with Technical College "Iuliu Maniu", Carei created a virtual space on www.edu.moodle.ro; the course page is listed as Satu Mare - Technical College "Iuliu Maniu", course: Baze de date Access BT
key_sources: Ioana Magdaş, Timea Bontea. (2011). Developing digital competences using an educational software. A pedagogical research. Acta Didactica Napocensia, Volume 4, Number 4, ISSN 2065-1430. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1056072

article_title: Efficacy of Interactive Whiteboard on Psychomotor Skills Achievement of Students in Isometric and Orthographic Projection
citation: Gambari, I. A., Balogun, S. A., & Alfa, A. S. (2014). Efficacy of Interactive Whiteboard on Psychomotor Skills Achievement of Students in Isometric and Orthographic Projection. Contemporary Educational Technology, 5(4), 316-330. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1124320
title: Basic Technology Achievement Test (BTAT)
description: The Basic Technology Achievement Test (BTAT) is a researcher-developed instrument used to measure psychomotor skills achievement in isometric and orthographic projection. It "consists of 25 -multiple-choice objective test items with five options (A -D)" and a bio-data section. It was validated by experts in Industrial and Technology Education, subject teachers, and test-and-measurement specialists, with reliability of 0.84 (KR-21).
requirements: Expert validation by technology education specialists, subject teachers, and test-and-measurement specialists
examples: Administered as pretest to ascertain equivalence before treatment and as posttest immediately after the four-week treatment
key_sources: Gambari, I. A., Balogun, S. A., & Alfa, A. S. (2014). Efficacy of Interactive Whiteboard on Psychomotor Skills Achievement of Students in Isometric and Orthographic Projection. Contemporary Educational Technology, 5(4), 316-330. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1105500
